review_notes: I read the whole file and checked its local definitions against Mathlib: valF, cQ, cHom, the local coeffEmb_rat and laurentBaseChange_rat, and the FibreIsoAux lemmas. I ignored the standalone theorems (injective_of_isField, isLocalization_away_of_irreducible_aux, finrank_adjoin_eq_of_eq, isIntegrallyClosed_of_mem_iff_isIntegral') because the rubric excludes theorem duplication. valF is the only clear competing definition: it re-defines the ring-hom inclusion of an IntermediateField that Mathlib already provides. cQ looks like a similar case, but I could not confirm that a Mathlib replacement exists, so I did not report it. The valF replacement has not been compiled. I did not check whether a ℚ-algebra structure on `FN` matches `IntermediateField.val` definitionally, so the exact `commutes'` proofs may need small adjustments.

findings.problem: `valF` is the coercion/inclusion of the intermediate field `qExpFunctionFieldC ℚ Γ` into `LaurentSeries ℚ`, built by hand. Mathlib already has this map as `IntermediateField.val : S →ₐ[K] L`, and the ring-hom version is `.toRingHom`. Because `valF` is only a ring hom, the file then needs `valF_algebraMap`, which is proved with a `Subsingleton.elim` on ring homs out of ℚ. With `IntermediateField.val` the statement `val (algebraMap ℚ FN q) = algebraMap ℚ (LaurentSeries ℚ) q` is just `AlgHom.commutes`.
findings.proposed_change: Delete `valF` and use `(qExpFunctionFieldC ℚ Γ).val` (as an `AlgHom`, or `.toRingHom` where a ring hom is needed). Define `eF` as `(coeffEmb Qb).comp (qExpFunctionFieldC ℚ Γ).val.toRingHom`, or as an `AlgHom` composition. Replace `valF_algebraMap` with `AlgHom.commutes` plus `algebraMap_laurent` or `HahnSeries.C`. The call sites at lines 250–251, 318–319 and 399 would then use standard simp and commutes lemmas.
findings.benefit: This removes a private copy of the standard subfield inclusion and an ad hoc `Subsingleton` proof. It lets the proofs use Mathlib's `IntermediateField.val` lemmas, and readers do not have to check that `valF` equals the usual inclusion.
